title: Zeo++ geometric pore characterization
action: Run Zeo++ on each of the six MFM frameworks (MFM-126,127,128,136,137,138) using appropriate probe radii: N₂ kinetic diameter (3.64 Å) for surface area, zero radius for accessible volume, and helium radius for void fraction. Compute pore limiting diameter (PLD), largest cavity diameter (LCD), total geometric surface area (sum of accessible and non-accessible), probe-occupiable volume (zero-radius probe), and helium void fraction. Write the results to structural_properties.json.
description: Geometric analysis step that produces the structural descriptors (PLD, LCD, surface area, volume, void fraction) for all six MFM MOFs.
output_schema: Array of 6 JSON objects, each with keys: 'mof' (string, MOF name), 'pld' (float, pore limiting diameter in Angstrom), 'lcd' (float, largest cavity diameter in Angstrom), 'lcd_pl' (float, LCD/PLD ratio), 'total_sa' (float, total geometric surface area in m²/g), 'volume' (float, probe-occupiable volume with zero-radius probe in cm³/g), 'void_fraction' (float, helium void fraction).

title: GCMC selectivity computation
action: Using RASPA, perform Grand Canonical Monte Carlo simulations for Xe and Kr single-component isotherms and for 50/50 and 20/80 binary mixture isotherms at 273 K and 298 K, over pressures from 0.01 bar to 10 bar. Use Dreiding+UFF force field for framework atoms (UFF for Cu) and published guest parameters (Hirschfelder for Xe, Talu–Myers for Kr). From the binary mixture uptake data, compute Xe/Kr selectivity at 0.01 bar and 10 bar for each combination of temperature and gas mixture. Output the resulting selectivities as selectivity_summary.json.
description: Main headline result: Xe/Kr selectivity values at 0.01 bar and 10 bar for all six MOFs under eight conditions (two temperatures × two mixture compositions × two pressures). Requires full execution of the GCMC simulation pipeline.
output_schema: JSON object with exactly 8 keys: 'S_50_50_273_0.01', 'S_50_50_273_10', 'S_50_50_298_0.01', 'S_50_50_298_10', 'S_20_80_273_0.01', 'S_20_80_273_10', 'S_20_80_298_0.01', 'S_20_80_298_10'. Each key maps to an object whose keys are MOF names (e.g. 'MFM-126') and values are the computed Xe/Kr selectivity (float).

title: Widom insertion for heats and Henry constants
action: Perform Widom insertion simulations (100,000 cycles) at 298 K in RASPA for each MOF to obtain infinite dilution heats of adsorption (Qst) for Xe and Kr, and Henry constants K_H for both gases. Compute Henry selectivity as K_H_Xe / K_H_Kr. Write the results to thermodynamic_properties.json.
description: Thermodynamic binding metrics: heats of adsorption and Henry constants, as reported in the paper. Requires Widom insertion simulations.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: 'Qst_Xe' (object mapping MOF name to float, kJ/mol), 'Qst_Kr' (object mapping MOF name to float, kJ/mol), 'K_H_Xe' (object mapping MOF name to float, units mol·kg⁻¹·Pa⁻¹ ×10⁻⁵), 'K_H_Kr' (object mapping MOF name to float, same units), 'Henry_selectivity' (object mapping MOF name to float, K_H_Xe / K_H_Kr).
